sections.hypothesis: Holding up to 3 altcoins chosen each week from the coins liquid at that date, by 90-day return, only while BTC closes more than 3% above its 50-day average and each coin is above its own close 30 days earlier, each sized to 50% volatility, and never holding a coin whose delisting has been announced or whose first perp listed in the last 30 days, beats holding the same coins at the same average exposure and the large-basket control, after costs.
sections.rationale: Who pays: in a crypto risk-on regime, money rotates into altcoins and trends persist (under-reaction, then late buyers chasing); when BTC turns down, alts fall harder, so a BTC gate keeps the portfolio out of most of their crashes. Evidence in Kestrel: btc-regime-trend passed its confirmation on 180 unsearched coins (findings 13); G1 (the same weekly rotation on 8 fixed large coins) passed a holdout year on 8 unseen coins (findings 15) but its own coin list is survivorship-biased; the two exit rules (delistings, findings 11; perp listings, findings 18) were found for exactly this portfolio. Outside evidence: crypto momentum (Liu, Tsyvinski and Wu 2022, Journal of Finance) and time-series momentum (Moskowitz, Ooi and Pedersen 2012). Disclosed: this extends G1 (pursued) and the rotation family (the plain monthly rotation on BTC/ETH/SOL was dropped after its holdout); the change that matters is a point-in-time universe, which fixes G1's survivorship. Implementation: altcoin-rotation (kestrel.strategies.altcoin_rotation; coin events from kestrel.data.coin_events). Runs: one scorecard run (1 trial), then the scorecard's robustness and walk-forward grids (each setting counted), then one holdout test.
sections.rules: Universe, decided at each Sunday close from what was known then (no survivors-only list): every Binance USDT spot coin of the exploration half of the split (the confirmation half stays locked: the engine refuses it, and lifting the lock is Luke's call), except BTC, ETH and SOL (their holdout is spent; BTC is read for the regime only), with at least 365 days of unbroken history and a median daily quote volume of at least 20M USDT over the last 30 days. Counted on 2026-11-21 before any return was read: a median of 14 coins a Sunday pass those filters (1 to 42), 2020-01 to 2025-10. Tokenized stocks (listed from 2026-06) can't have a year of history by 2026-10, so the history rule keeps them out of the holdout year too. Regime: BTC's close more than 3% above its 50-day average. Choice: among eligible coins whose close is above their close 30 days earlier, the top 3 by 90-day return; each held at 1/3 x min(1, 50% / its annualised volatility of the last 30 daily log returns); the rest in cash; outside the regime, all cash. Exit rules, checked daily at each close: a coin whose delisting was announced (Binance's announcements, kestrel.data.delistings, stored from 2022-02: earlier delistings get only the engine's forced sale at the last close) is sold at the next open and not bought again; a coin whose first USDT-M perp settled funding in the last 30 days is not bought, and a held one is sold at the next open (the funding archive starts 2020-01, so a perp first seen then counts as old, never new). Decisions at the Sunday close, traded at Monday's open through the portfolio engine, daily bars, kestrel.toml costs (each coin's spread band, BNB fee rate), the no-trade band, Binance's 5 USDT minimum, 330 USDT.
sections.falsification: The full scorecard (CLAUDE.md), on 2020-01-01 to 2025-10-31: Sharpe beats the same coins at the same average exposure (here: the large-basket control on the same exploration-half universe, held at the strategy's average exposure) and the large-basket control, after costs; deflated Sharpe >= 95% on the main trial count; walk-forward: most test windows beat exposure-matched holding; at least half of the 2-year start windows beat it; break-even cost >= 2x actual; at least 30 trades; max drawdown <= 50%; neighbouring settings (top 2 and 4; 60 and 120-day ranking; 2% and 4% margins) also pass test 1. If it passes every test but luck, as the pursued strategies do, Claude recommends a holdout test (2025-11 to 2026-10, run once with kestrel holdout-test, on the same point-in-time universe), and Luke decides. Failing test 1 or the drawdown limit is a drop recommendation; Luke decides.
sections.parameters: top_n 3, lookback_days 90, btc_days 50, margin_pct 3, coin_days 30, vol_days 30, target_vol_pct 50, min_volume 20M USDT, min_history 365 days, perp_exit_days 30. G1's settings, fixed before any run of this rule; the robustness grid tries the neighbours above and counts each as a trial.
sections.costs: kestrel.toml: 7.5 bps taker fee (BNB discount), each coin's half-spread band by its 30-day median volume, square-root impact, Binance's 5 USDT minimum (a slot of about 35-110 USDT clears it). A forced delisting sale pays the coin's band like any other. Weekly decisions keep turnover low; the scorecard's break-even cost test checks the margin.
